column1: What is the primary intended purpose of an HTTP GET request?
column2: An HTTP GET request is intended to retrieve data from a server.

column1: What is the primary intended purpose of an HTTP POST request?
column2: An HTTP POST request is intended to send data to a server for processing.

column1: Where are request parameters placed in an HTTP GET request?
column2: Parameters in an HTTP GET request are appended directly within the URL.

column1: Where are request parameters placed in an HTTP POST request?
column2: Parameters in an HTTP POST request are enclosed inside the request body.

column1: How do parameter size limits compare between HTTP GET and POST requests?
column2: HTTP GET requests face browser-enforced length limits, whereas HTTP POST requests have no payload size limit.

column1: Why is storing sensitive parameters like API keys in an HTTP GET request considered insecure?
column2: URLs are recorded in browser history, bookmarks, and server logs, exposing sensitive parameters.

column1: What is the main function of HTTP request headers during API interactions?
column2: Request headers provide additional context and metadata to the server, such as authentication credentials and client details.

column1: What information does the Content-Type HTTP request header convey to a server?
column2: The Content-Type header informs the server about the exact format of the data contained in the request body.

column1: What is the purpose of the User-Agent HTTP request header during web scraping?
column2: The User-Agent header identifies the client browser, operating system, and device details to the server.

column1: What general outcome is indicated by an HTTP response status code in the 2xx range?
column2: HTTP 2xx status codes indicate that the client request was successfully received, understood, and accepted.

column1: What condition does the HTTP status code 200 OK represent?
column2: The HTTP 200 OK status code represents the standard successful completion of an HTTP request.

column1: What category of HTTP responses is denoted by status codes in the 3xx range?
column2: HTTP 3xx status codes denote redirection messages requiring further action from the client.

column1: What type of issues do HTTP status codes in the 4xx range indicate?
column2: HTTP 4xx status codes indicate errors originating from an invalid or unauthorized client request.

column1: What failure condition produces an HTTP 400 Bad Request status code?
column2: An HTTP 400 Bad Request status code indicates that the server cannot process the request due to malformed client syntax.

column1: How does an HTTP 401 Unauthorized status code differ from an HTTP 403 Forbidden status code?
column2: An HTTP 401 code denotes missing or invalid credentials, whereas an HTTP 403 code denotes that access is denied despite authentication.

column1: What scenario triggers an HTTP 404 Not Found response code?
column2: An HTTP 404 response code occurs when the server cannot locate the requested resource at the specified URL.

column1: What broad class of failure is denoted by HTTP response status codes in the 5xx range?
column2: HTTP 5xx status codes denote server-side failures where the server fails to complete an apparently valid request.

column1: What error condition triggers an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error response?
column2: An HTTP 500 response indicates an unexpected generic error on the server side that prevents request processing.

column1: What condition causes a server to return an HTTP 503 Service Unavailable status code?
column2: An HTTP 503 status code indicates that the server is temporarily incapable of handling requests due to overload or maintenance.

column1: What is the difference between internal and external data sources?
column2: Internal data is captured by an organisation's own systems (e.g., a Point-of-Sale system); external data comes from third-party APIs, web scraping or partners' databases.

column1: What does the acronym CRUD stand for?
column2: Create, Read, Update, Delete: the basic database operations used to capture internal data.

column1: Why is a RESTful API described as stateless?
column2: Each request is independent: one request receives one complete response.

column1: Why is a streaming API described as stateful?
column2: Messages are usually deltas (changes), so the client must maintain state built from previous messages.

column1: Name three API types other than RESTful and streaming.
column2: FIX (Financial Information eXchange), SOAP, and GraphQL.

column1: What are the three main concerns when relying on a third-party data API?
column2: Rate limiting, data availability (not all data is offered via the API), and data quality.

column1: Is HTTP POST more secure than GET because it encrypts the request body?
column2: No. Encryption depends on HTTPS, which both GET and POST can use; POST's advantage is only that parameters are not in the logged URL.

column1: Where should an API key usually be placed in an HTTP request?
column2: In the request headers, as specified by the API documentation.

column1: In a Pub/Sub system, does a producer know how many consumers subscribe to its topic?
column2: No. Producers push event records to a topic without knowing how many consumers have subscribed.

column1: How many parties are involved in Pub/Sub versus a Webhook?
column2: Pub/Sub has three (producer, broker, consumer); a Webhook has two (source and destination).

column1: Which delivery models does Pub/Sub support compared with a Webhook?
column2: Pub/Sub supports pull or push; a Webhook is push-only.

column1: In an HTML page, how are images provided?
column2: HTML is a text file that uses tags to structure content; image data are provided in external files.

column1: How does a crawler read all pages of one website?
column2: It extracts links from each page, visits those on the same domain, and avoids visiting the same link twice (e.g., with Scrapy).

column1: What are the trade-offs of converting a whole webpage to plain text (e.g., with Beautiful Soup)?
column2: It is generic but yields unstructured data of limited clarity; it is often used for the web-browsing function of text-only LLMs.

column1: What mechanism do Selenium and Playwright rely on to control a browser?
column2: Browsers' native automation capabilities (built for automated testing), exposed through a Python API.

column1: How can CAPTCHA solving be framed technically?
column2: As a machine learning problem (e.g., image or audio classification).
